runs.text: 1. Reported leverage is moderate and stable. Net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA was between 1.20x and 1.31x at the four quarter-ends from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026, and 1.28x at the latest; total debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA was 1.33x [CP-1]. The issuer targets a sustained net debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratio of below 1.0x, so the calculated ratio is above its own target [CP-1A]. Because the debt is in US dollars and statements in Canadian dollars, the carrying value rose by CAD 22.9 million from exchange rates over the nine months even as CAD 75.1 million was repaid, so the Canadian dollar balance understates progress [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact for the reported items, Analyst Interpretation for the ratios. 2. Free cash flow weakened. The issuer's cash from operations of CAD 279.5 million for nine months 2026 funded capital expenditure of CAD 223.8 million, up 22.9% on the prior-year nine months, leaving free cash flow of CAD 55.7 million after CAD 104.7 million the year before; in Q3 2026 alone free cash flow was negative CAD 11.7 million [CP-1]. Mechanism: expansion and upgrade spending, reactivation costs and seasonal working-capital builds absorb cash while Adjusted EBITDA is lower than the prior-year nine months. Implication: shareholder returns of CAD 46.6 million and net debt repayment of CAD 75.1 million were funded partly by running cash down to CAD 23.2 million. Category: Analyst Interpretation. 3. Liquidity is adequate but depends on the revolver. The issuer reports more than CAD 460 million of available liquidity and the recomputation gives CAD 462.5 million, of which about CAD 382 million is undrawn revolver [CP-1]. Letters of credit consume revolver availability and US$43 million of commitments expire on June 28, 2027. Category: Analyst Interpretation. 4. Refinancing is concentrated in 2028 and 2029. US$46 million of revolver is drawn to October 31, 2028 and US$400 million of 6.875% unsecured notes mature on January 15, 2029, about 90% of principal. Nothing in the supplied sources shows redemption terms, the notes' pricing history or the terms of the revolver's extension option [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact for dates, Insufficient Information for terms. 5. Covenants are not constraining on reported numbers: senior secured debt to covenant EBITDA of 0.14x against a 2.50x ceiling, and covenant EBITDA to interest of 10.27x against a 2.50x floor. The covenant EBITDA definition and the notes' coverage value are not supplied, so the reported ratios cannot be recomputed [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact; limitation stated. 6. Business risk is cyclical with partial contract support. Revenue is almost all day-rate or hourly; term-contracted average rigs were 54 in Q3 2026 against 40 a year earlier, all seven international rigs are on five-year contracts running into 2027 and 2028, but in Q1 2026 term-contracted rigs generated only 26% of Canadian and 34% of United States utilization days [CP-1A]. Category: Documentary Fact. 7. A contested tax reassessment is a contingent cash call. The Canada Revenue Agency denied a deduction for the 2018 tax year and proposed the same for 2019 to 2022; the issuer estimates a maximum tax liability of about CAD 155 million excluding interest, recognizes no liability, and must pay half of any assessed amount while contesting [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact; outcome and timing are uncertain. 8. Governance behaviour is supportive on deleveraging and mixed on distributions: the issuer reduced debt and targets CAD 100 million of reduction for 2026, and also allocates up to 50% of free cash flow before debt repayments to buybacks, with cash at a low level; no extraction or creditor-adverse action is documented, but legal capacity under the debt agreements is not visible [CP-1A]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA grew in Q3 2026 against Q3 2025, while nine-month Adjusted EBITDA is lower than the prior-year nine months, because of lower upfront capital payments in Canada, higher operating costs in the United States and internationally, and higher share-based compensation (R3 page:5). Leverage computed from reported figures is steady and moderate, interest cover on a nine-month basis improved, and covenant headroom is wide. The limits are equally clear: free cash flow weakened as capital spending rose, cash is small, liquidity is revolver-dependent, a contested tax reassessment is a contingent cash call, and the annual comparators, the covenant EBITDA definition and the facility pricing are not in the pack. fields.value: The supplied sources describe a publicly listed Canadian contract driller with no sponsor, no parent and no disclosed controlling holder, and with no acquisition, disposal, recapitalisation or new debt issue in the period. The business is two segments: Contract Drilling Services, which earns day-rate revenue from drilling rigs in Canada, the United States and the Middle East, and Completion and Production Services, which earns hourly and rental revenue in Canada. Volume depends on oil and gas prices and customer capital discipline; Canadian volume is seasonal because spring break-up halts heavy equipment moves. Term contracts add visibility, and coverage rose during 2026, but contracted rigs are less than half of the average active fleet, and in Q1 2026, the only quarter for which the share of utilization days is disclosed, term-contracted rigs generated a minority of days in both Canada and the United States, where reactivation costs are also depressing 2026 margins. Management describes a step change in United States margins in the fourth quarter; that is management language, not a result. For a creditor the operating story matters through four mechanics: oil-price-driven activity swings feed through to cash flow quickly because costs are largely variable; capital spending is discretionary but was raised twice in 2026, first for contracted upgrades and then for long-lead deliveries and a pending upgrade; international rigs are fully contracted but concentrated in two markets near a conflict zone; and capital allocation splits free cash flow between debt repayment and buybacks, with cash drawn down. The pack cannot show who controls the company, how concentrated customers are, how the notes came to exist, or what the credit agreement permits in distributions, so legal capacity and willingness to prioritise creditors are only partly assessable.

Evidence: term-contracted average rigs rose for 2026 and all international rigs are on five-year contracts (R3 pages 7 and 8), but the United States term share of utilization days fell in Q1 2026 (R1 page:8). Mechanic: day-rate revenue follows activity, which follows oil prices and customer budgets; term contracts floor part of it and shortfall payments are small. Implication: a commodity downturn would cut United States and Canadian volumes faster than costs fall in the first months, so cash flow and revolver reliance would rise; term coverage limits but does not remove this. Evidence: United States reactivation costs per day rose and guidance expects a step change in the fourth quarter (R3 pages 4 and 7); share-based compensation is cash-settled and share-price sensitive (R3 page:11). Mechanic: reactivation spending is front-loaded and is recovered only if utilization and day rates hold; compensation expense moves EBITDA with the share price. Implication: current-year EBITDA understates or overstates run-rate depending on both; the fourth-quarter guidance should be monitored, not assumed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Precision Drilling is a moderately leveraged North American driller with sound reported credit metrics but a cyclical business and a thin cash cushion. Its strongest support is reported net debt of 1.28x LTM Adjusted EBITDA, covenant ratios far inside their limits and CAD 462.5 million of recomputed liquidity. Its weakest point is free cash flow: CAD 55.7 million for nine months 2026 against CAD 104.7 million a year earlier, while debt repayment and buybacks totalled CAD 121.6 million and cash fell to CAD 23.2 million. The outcome turns on oil-driven North American activity, the United States margin recovery management guides to, refinancing of the 2028 revolver and 2029 notes, and the Canada Revenue Agency reassessment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Reported leverage is moderate and stable. Net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA was between 1.20x and 1.31x at the four quarter-ends from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026, and 1.28x at the latest; total debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA was 1.33x [CP-1]. The issuer targets a sustained net debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratio of below 1.0x, so the calculated ratio is above its own target [CP-1A]. Because the debt is in US dollars and statements in Canadian dollars, the carrying value rose by CAD 22.9 million from exchange rates over the nine months even as CAD 75.1 million was repaid, so the Canadian dollar balance understates progress [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact for the reported items, Analyst Interpretation for the ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Free cash flow weakened. The issuer's cash from operations of CAD 279.5 million for nine months 2026 funded capital expenditure of CAD 223.8 million, up 22.9% on the prior-year nine months, leaving free cash flow of CAD 55.7 million after CAD 104.7 million the year before; in Q3 2026 alone free cash flow was negative CAD 11.7 million [CP-1]. Mechanism: expansion and upgrade spending, reactivation costs and seasonal working-capital builds absorb cash while Adjusted EBITDA is lower than the prior-year nine months. Implication: shareholder returns of CAD 46.6 million and net debt repayment of CAD 75.1 million were funded partly by running cash down to CAD 23.2 million. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Liquidity is adequate but depends on the revolver. The issuer reports more than CAD 460 million of available liquidity and the recomputation gives CAD 462.5 million, of which about CAD 382 million is undrawn revolver [CP-1]. Letters of credit consume revolver availability and US$43 million of commitments expire on June 28, 2027. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Refinancing is concentrated in 2028 and 2029. US$46 million of revolver is drawn to October 31, 2028 and US$400 million of 6.875% unsecured notes mature on January 15, 2029, about 90% of principal. Nothing in the supplied sources shows redemption terms, the notes' pricing history or the terms of the revolver's extension option [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact for dates, Insufficient Information for terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Covenants are not constraining on reported numbers: senior secured debt to covenant EBITDA of 0.14x against a 2.50x ceiling, and covenant EBITDA to interest of 10.27x against a 2.50x floor. The covenant EBITDA definition and the notes' coverage value are not supplied, so the reported ratios cannot be recomputed [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact; limitation stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Business risk is cyclical with partial contract support. Revenue is almost all day-rate or hourly; term-contracted average rigs were 54 in Q3 2026 against 40 a year earlier, all seven international rigs are on five-year contracts running into 2027 and 2028, but in Q1 2026 term-contracted rigs generated only 26% of Canadian and 34% of United States utilization days [CP-1A]. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. A contested tax reassessment is a contingent cash call. The Canada Revenue Agency denied a deduction for the 2018 tax year and proposed the same for 2019 to 2022; the issuer estimates a maximum tax liability of about CAD 155 million excluding interest, recognizes no liability, and must pay half of any assessed amount while contesting [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact; outcome and timing are uncertain.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 8. Governance behaviour is supportive on deleveraging and mixed on distributions: the issuer reduced debt and targets CAD 100 million of reduction for 2026, and also allocates up to 50% of free cash flow before debt repayments to buybacks, with cash at a low level; no extraction or creditor-adverse action is documented, but legal capacity under the debt agreements is not visible [CP-1A]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.
